mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 50% of the time when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, indicating no positive effect.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts reflects strong consumer demand and economic expansion, positively influencing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Housing starts rise but SPX 60-day returns are negative, indicating no positive demand impact.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 6% but SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth but negative SPX 60-day returns, indicating no supply impact.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rate decreases and payroll employment increases, it signals a robust labor market, boosting equity returns.
failure_condition: Both UNRATE and PAYEMS improve but SPX 20-day returns are negative in over 50% cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate above a threshold may signal monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% but SPX 5-day returns remain positive, indicating no negative impact.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing real consumer spending reflects strong demand, positively influencing corporate revenues and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth but negative SPX 20-day returns, indicating no demand effect.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, slowing GDP growth may lead to caution in equity markets, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth below 2% but positive SPX 60-day returns, indicating no late-cycle impact.
